experimento_investigacion: Apollo 13 (CSM-109 / LM-7)
instalacion_hardware: Apollo CSM-109 Service Module (Oxygen Tank 2) / LM-7 Aquarius
investigador_responsable: NASA SMA / Apollo 13 Review Board (Cortright Commission)
fecha_periodo: 1970-04 (third day of the mission; splashdown 17 Apr 1970)
material_combustible: Cryogenic oxygen; Teflon wiring insulation
condiciones: Heaters on for ~8 h up to ~1000 °F (final pad test); 65 V DC
descripcion_objetivo: Oxygen tank 2 exploded: heaters raised from 28 to 65 V DC without upgrading the thermostats; overheating during the pad test damaged the insulation
consecuencia_hallazgo: Damage to tank 1, loss of fuel cells, power and water; lunar mission aborted; crew returned alive using the lunar module as a lifeboat
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add a third O2 tank isolated in another compartment; 2) Upgrade thermostats to withstand 65 V DC; 3) Remove mechanical stirring fans inside O2 tanks; 4) Encase wiring in stainless-steel sheathing; 5) Reform detanking test procedures and manufacturing change control.

experimento_investigacion: Apollo 1 (AS-204, CM-012)
investigador_responsable: NASA SMA / Apollo 204 Review Board
material_combustible: Combustible materials inside the cabin (nylon, Velcro, foam); pure oxygen atmosphere
condiciones: Cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen (16.7 psi), hatches closed, suits on; three-piece hatch that took ~90 s to open under ideal conditions
descripcion_objetivo: Sudden fire in the command module during an internal-power test (Plugs-Out Test); evidence of electrical arcing in vulnerable wiring near the environmental control system
consecuencia_hallazgo: Three astronauts died of CO and toxic-gas asphyxiation; pressure vessel ruptured; test wrongly classified as non-hazardous, with no rescue protocol
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign a unified quick-opening hatch (opens outward in 3 s from inside or outside); 2) Replace the 100% O2 launch atmosphere with a 60% O2 / 40% N2 mix on the pad; 3) Strictly restrict and relocate combustible materials (Velcro, nylon) and adopt Beta cloth fabrics / fire-resistant suits; 4) Shield wiring and plumbing to the Block II standard; 5) Mandatory hazardous-test protocols with on-site rescue.

experimento_investigacion: FLEX - Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams / Forman Williams & Dietrich (NASA GRC)
material_combustible: Heptane and methanol droplets
condiciones: O2/N2 diluted with N2, CO2, He or Xe; 1-5 mm droplets; 0-3 atm; up to 40% O2
descripcion_objetivo: See how an inert suppressant gas changes the flammability limit
consecuencia_hallazgo: Lower flammability limit in microgravity; terrestrial inert-suppressant standards do not give the same safety margin; cool flames were observed after the visible flame went out
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Raise the minimum concentrations of inert suppressant gases (N2, CO2, He) above terrestrial standards; 2) Add infrared/spectral sensors to detect invisible cool flames and keep post-extinction monitoring to prevent spontaneous reignition.

experimento_investigacion: FLEX-2 - Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
investigador_responsable: NASA GRC Combustion Science Team
material_combustible: Fuel blends, real-fuel surrogates, biofuels
condiciones: Slow convective flow effects, droplet-droplet interaction, droplet arrays
descripcion_objetivo: Study soot formation, fuel range and flame spread across droplet arrays
consecuencia_hallazgo: Basis for studying combustion of practical liquid fuels and flame spread between neighbouring droplets
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update engine and thruster kinetic models with slow radiative and convective droplet-droplet coupling; 2) Adjust injection spacing in droplet arrays to mitigate soot and reignition.

experimento_investigacion: SPICE - Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
material_combustible: Gaseous fuels in coflow
condiciones: Axisymmetric laminar flame
descripcion_objetivo: Transition from soot-free to sooting flame (smoke point)
consecuencia_hallazgo: The smoke point indicates a fuel's tendency to produce soot and thermal radiation in microgravity
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalibrate smoke-point thresholds in buoyancy-free laminar burners; 2) Keep fuel flow below the soot-release threshold to avoid radiative losses and filter clogging on the ISS.

experimento_investigacion: SLICE - Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigador_responsable: M. B. Long (Yale)
material_combustible: Combustibles gaseosos
condiciones: Lifted flames at different coflow rates
descripcion_objetivo: Structure of lifted flames; improve efficiency and reduce pollutants
consecuencia_hallazgo: Precursor of CLD Flame; characterizes stabilization of a flame base detached from the nozzle
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Adjust coflow velocity and nozzle geometry to stabilize lifted flames without blow-off; 2) Integrate the high-resolution optical diagnostics later implemented in ACME CLD Flame.

experimento_investigacion: LSP - Laminar Soot Processes
investigador_responsable: G. Faeth (U. Michigan)
material_combustible: Gases (etileno, propano)
condiciones: Sealed chamber, quiescent environment
descripcion_objetivo: Soot formation and oxidation in quiescent diffusion flames
consecuencia_hallazgo: Reference data for soot formation/destruction models without buoyant acceleration
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include long-residence-time soot radiation in CFD combustion models; 2) Tune cabin optical detectors and filters for primary soot aggregates larger than in 1 g.

experimento_investigacion: TGDF - Turbulent Gas-jet Diffusion Flame
investigador_responsable: M. Y. Bahadori (SAIC)
material_combustible: Propane/hydrogen gas
condiciones: Sealed chamber; iris that induces vortices in the air
descripcion_objetivo: Flame-vortex interaction and stability in turbulent jets
consecuencia_hallazgo: Improves understanding of momentum-dominated turbulent combustion without buoyancy
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Remove buoyancy turbulent-production terms from k-epsilon / LES models for microgravity; 2) Redesign jet injectors for the longer turbulent flame length in 0 g.

experimento_investigacion: ELF - Enclosed Laminar Flames
investigador_responsable: L. D. Chen (U. Iowa)
material_combustible: Gas metano/propano
condiciones: Duct with fan (forced coflow)
descripcion_objetivo: Stability of a laminar flame confined in a duct
consecuencia_hallazgo: SLICE is its second generation; it showed the role of confinement and coflow in liftoff height
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Evolve the confined wind tunnel into the modular SPICE/SLICE architecture in the MSG; 2) Control the duct-wall boundary layer to avoid disturbing the flame base.

experimento_investigacion: BRE - Burning Rate Emulator (ACME)
investigador_responsable: J. G. Quintiere (U. Maryland)
material_combustible: Flat porous burner with gaseous fuel that mimics paper, plastic and alcohol
condiciones: Fuel flow controlled by heat flux and surface temperature
descripcion_objetivo: Understand ignition and extinction of materials and evaluate flammability tests in low gravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Focused on spacecraft fire prevention by emulating the heat of vaporization of solids with gas
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Calibrate the feedback between surface thermocouples, radiant heat-flux sensors and the gas mass-flow valve to emulate the mass-transfer B-number of real polymers in space habitats.

experimento_investigacion: CLD Flame - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME)
investigador_responsable: M. B. Long (Yale)
material_combustible: Methane and ethylene diluted in air coflow
condiciones: Highly diluted and highly sooting flames; lifted flames
descripcion_objetivo: Verify kinetic and soot models at dilution extremes
consecuencia_hallazgo: Applicable to ignition limits and flame stability in extreme regimes
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Extend detailed chemical mechanisms for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) precursors and soot to high N2-dilution regimes.

experimento_investigacion: E-FIELD Flames - Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME)
investigador_responsable: D. Dunn-Rankin (UC Irvine)
material_combustible: Coflow or simple jet flame (methane/ethylene)
condiciones: Electric field up to 10 kV
descripcion_objetivo: Use ions to control diffusion flames through ionic wind
consecuencia_hallazgo: Measure ion current and flame response; makes it possible to emulate convection equivalent to partial gravity without thermal buoyancy
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Install high-voltage electrode meshes (up to 10 kV) to induce forced convection by ionic wind, reducing soot formation and allowing lunar/Martian gravity (0.16 g - 0.38 g) to be emulated.

experimento_investigacion: Flame Design - Flame Design (ACME)
investigador_responsable: R. L. Axelbaum (Washington U.)
material_combustible: Ethylene or methane in an O2-enriched atmosphere
condiciones: Spherical flames; possible inverse spherical flame if safety approves
descripcion_objetivo: Soot inception and design of robust soot-free flames
consecuencia_hallazgo: Determination of soot and flammability limits by controlling the stoichiometric structure
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Reconfigure burner stoichiometry (shifting the oxidizer or diluent) to run in O2-enriched atmospheres with strong flames free of soot and excess radiation.

experimento_investigacion: s-Flame - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME)
investigador_responsable: C. K. Law (Princeton)
material_combustible: Hydrogen and methane (soot-free); ethylene (sooting)
condiciones: Spherical porous burner; various diluents
descripcion_objetivo: Radiative and convective extinction limits; pulsating instabilities
consecuencia_hallazgo: A one-dimensional spherical flame, possible only in microgravity; reveals pulsating instabilities before radiative extinction
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include gas radiative losses (CO2, H2O) and Lewis-number coupling in extinction models of large spherical flames in space habitats.

experimento_investigacion: BASS - Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson / P. Ferkul (NASA GRC)
material_combustible: Flat samples, PMMA spheres, porous wax sheets, wax candles, cotton/fiberglass fabrics
condiciones: Nominal air 21% O2, 1 atm; tests down to 17% O2; variable flow (0-35 cm/s); nitrogen suppression
descripcion_objetivo: Burning and extinction of solids; improve 1 g safety tests and extinction strategies
consecuencia_hallazgo: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative; materials burn at lower O2 in microgravity; a local nitrogen jet can strengthen the flame
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Revise NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward burning in 1 g) because it underestimates flammability in microgravity at low flows (~1-10 cm/s); 2) Prohibit applying slow localized N2 jets directly at the flame base without first cutting HVAC ventilation, since entrained O2 intensifies the fire.

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE - Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
instalacion_hardware: CIR (insert) + flow duct in the MSG (ISS)
investigador_responsable: NASA GRC SoFIE Project Team (P. Ferkul, S. Olson et al.)
material_combustible: Plastics such as PMMA or Delrin
condiciones: 10-40% O2; 0.2-1.5 atm; flow 0-30 cm/s (spacecraft ventilation range)
descripcion_objetivo: Characterize ignition and flammability of spacecraft materials in exploration atmospheres (e.g. 10.2 psi, 32-34% O2)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Umbrella program of five investigations to certify materials for the Artemis and Mars missions
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Certify all cabin polymers (PMMA, Delrin, fabrics) under low-pressure, high-O2 exploration atmospheres (up to 40% O2 and 0.2-1.5 atm) with real HVAC ventilation flows (0-30 cm/s).

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Flammability correlation - Correlation of Flammability between Normal and Microgravity
investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
material_combustible: Spacecraft engineering materials
condiciones: Variable oxygen, pressure and flow
descripcion_objetivo: Microgravity flammability map and comparison with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
consecuencia_hallazgo: Drop-tower data suggest NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace the single pass/fail criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with multidimensional maps of the maximum oxygen concentration (MOC) as a function of forced-flow velocity and pressure.

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Growth and extinction - Fundamentals of Flame Growth and Extinction in Microgravity
investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
material_combustible: Solid plastic spheres (PMMA)
condiciones: Gravity, flow, O2, pressure, size, preheating
descripcion_objetivo: Complete history of flame growth, spread and decay
consecuencia_hallazgo: Links 1 g flammability to microgravity through a canonical spherical geometry
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include the solid's internal preheating and surface curvature in predictive radiative-extinction models.

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Thermal and species fields - Thermal and Species Field Effects on Material Flammability
investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
material_combustible: Thin solid fuels
condiciones: Fuel thickness and ambient pressure
descripcion_objetivo: Separate flame spread due to the thermal field from that due to the species field (radiative extinction)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Can define the critical thickness, velocity or O2 for a material to be intrinsically safe
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Set minimum safe thicknesses for cabin coatings and plastic films below the thermal/species spread threshold.

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: External heat flux - External Heat Flux Effects on Ignitability and Suppression of Materials in Microgravity
investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
material_combustible: Materials in exploration atmospheres
condiciones: Low forced flow with external radiant heat
descripcion_objetivo: Ignition time and time to extinction after applying a suppressant
consecuencia_hallazgo: The critical heat flux for ignition in microgravity can be half that in normal gravity
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Cut the maximum allowed radiant heat flux near electronics and cables in spacecraft by 50% relative to the terrestrial standard; 2) Increase thermal insulation in power racks.

experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Narrow Channel - Narrow Channel as a 1-g Flammability Test Method
investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson / SoFIE Science Team
material_combustible: Representative thick solid fuel
condiciones: Opposed flow, O2 and pressure
descripcion_objetivo: See whether a narrow channel in 1 g reproduces flammability in microgravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Possible ground test that mimics microgravity flames by suppressing buoyant plumes
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Adopt the Narrow Channel Apparatus in ground laboratories as a standard complementary method to, or replacement for, NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 to pre-certify space materials in 1 g.

experimento_investigacion: SAME - Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
material_combustible: Smoke from spacecraft materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone, cellulose, overloaded lamp)
condiciones: Particle size distribution and aerosol aging in microgravity
descripcion_objetivo: Guide the design of space smoke detectors
consecuencia_hallazgo: Smoke particles in microgravity differ from terrestrial ones (more agglomeration due to the lack of buoyancy)
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign the laser-scattering optical chambers and threshold algorithms of space smoke detectors (Orion/Gateway/Lunar Lander) to detect the larger particle distributions produced by slow pyrolysis in 0 g.

experimento_investigacion: DAFT - Dust Aerosol measurement Feasibility Test
investigador_responsable: NASA GRC Aerosol Team
fecha_periodo: Recent (year not stated in the guide)
material_combustible: Background aerosols and dust on the ISS
condiciones: Background particle levels in the cabin
descripcion_objetivo: Measure background aerosol to reduce false alarms
consecuencia_hallazgo: Fast detection with few false alarms by discriminating ambient dust from real smoke
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add multi-wavelength discriminating filtering and lunar/ambient dust rejection to fire sensors to avoid false alarms from suspended dust after EVAs.

experimento_investigacion: Mist - Water Mist Fire Suppression experiment
investigador_responsable: T. McKinnon (Colorado School of Mines)
material_combustible: Premixed flame in a tube, several fuel/oxygen mixtures
condiciones: Water droplet diameter and concentration
descripcion_objetivo: Effectiveness of water mist in suppressing fire (replacement for Halon and CO2)
consecuencia_hallazgo: The first two of nine water-mist Portable Fire Extinguishers (PFE) reached the ISS in Dec. 2015 to replace the CO2 units
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace CO2 and Halon 1301 extinguishers with fine water-mist extinguishers (Water Mist PFE, droplets < 50 microns), removing the CO2 toxicity risk in a closed cabin.

experimento_investigacion: SOFBALL - Structure of Flame Balls at Low Lewis-number
investigador_responsable: P. Ronney (USC)
material_combustible: Mezclas premezcladas muy pobres (H2/O2/diluyente)
condiciones: Low Lewis number
descripcion_objetivo: Study stationary flame balls controlled by diffusion and radiation
consecuencia_hallazgo: The weakest flames ever burned (~1 W); some lasted more than 40 min without going out
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Lower the design lower flammability limit (LFL) for hydrogen and light-gas (low Lewis number) leaks in space habitats, since they can sustain stationary ~1 W flame balls below the terrestrial limit.

experimento_investigacion: Candle Flames - Candle Flames in non-buoyant atmospheres
investigador_responsable: D. L. Dietrich et al. (NASA GRC)
material_combustible: Paraffin candle
condiciones: Long-duration microgravity, quiescent air
descripcion_objetivo: Verify whether a flame can exist without natural convection
consecuencia_hallazgo: Burned for more than 45 min as a faint blue hemisphere and at lower O2 than on Earth; oscillates as it nears extinction
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Drop the assumption that turning off ventilation immediately self-extinguishes a fire in quiescent air; 2) Keep thermal/UV monitoring for faint blue hemispherical flames that persist by pure diffusion.

experimento_investigacion: SCWM - Super-Critical Water Mixture
investigador_responsable: NASA-CNES Joint Team
material_combustible: Mezcla agua-Na2SO4 (0.5% p/v)
condiciones: Above the critical point (T > 374 °C, P > 22.1 MPa), with temperature gradients
descripcion_objetivo: Formation and transport of salt precipitates in supercritical water
consecuencia_hallazgo: Relevant to SCWO (supercritical water oxidation) reactors for life support and waste recycling
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign walls and flow in life-support (ECLSS) SCWO reactors to avoid clogging and corrosion from inorganic salt (Na2SO4) precipitation without gravitational settling.

experimento_investigacion: Cool Flames (initiative) - Cool Flames in the CIR
investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams / Nayagam / Dietrich
material_combustible: Several fuel types (heavy alkanes, heptane, decane)
condiciones: Variable pressure and diluent concentration
descripcion_objetivo: Conditions before the hot/cool flame transition, stability and spontaneous reignition
consecuencia_hallazgo: Very weak flames (500-800 K), invisible to the naked eye, can reignite long after the visible flame went out
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update post-fire procedures on the ISS/Artemis to require full cooling and controlled venting of partially oxidized vapours (formaldehyde/CO) before reopening compartments where a flame seemed to go out.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Flammability limit (FLEX, BASS)
investigador_responsable: FLEX and BASS hardware
material_combustible: Heptane/methanol droplets and polymeric/cellulosic solids
condiciones: Microgravity with low convective flow
descripcion_objetivo: The flammability limit is lower in microgravity (heptane/methanol droplets and some solids)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Terrestrial standards do not give the same safety margin
modificaciones_necesarias: Lower the maximum allowed oxygen threshold (MOC) in space-material certification tables by an extra 2-4% O2 relative to 1 g ground tests.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 standard test (BASS)
investigador_responsable: Equipo BASS / SoFIE
material_combustible: Materiales certificados bajo NASA-STD-6001
condiciones: Comparison of 1 g upward burning vs 0 g with slow forced flow
descripcion_objetivo: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative: materials burn at lower oxygen in microgravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Ground tests can underestimate the fire risk in orbit
modificaciones_necesarias: Replace or complement NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with slow opposed-flow tests and a Narrow Channel apparatus calibrated with BASS and SoFIE data.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Spread against the flow (RITS / BASS)
investigador_responsable: Radiative Ignition and Transition to Spread / BASS
material_combustible: Thin and thick solids
condiciones: Low forced flow (< 10 cm/s) in microgravity
descripcion_objetivo: At low flow the flame spreads against the flow (upwind, toward fresh oxygen), the opposite of normal gravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Changes how fire spread is modelled and where to place sensors/firebreaks in spacecraft
modificaciones_necesarias: Reverse the geometry of firebreak barriers and the placement of thermal sensors in ducts/racks so they also watch upstream (toward the ventilation air inlet).
fuente: Radiative Ignition and Transition to Spread (NASA Guide 2015)

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Spacecraft ventilation (~10 cm/s)
investigador_responsable: Flame-spread studies over solids (BASS)
material_combustible: Cabin polymers and fabrics
condiciones: Typical cabin ventilation velocity (~10 cm/s)
descripcion_objetivo: ~10 cm/s (typical ventilation velocity) coincides with the minimum of the flammability curve and the maximum spread
consecuencia_hallazgo: Nominal spacecraft ventilation worsens a fire and maximizes the burning rate
modificaciones_necesarias: Automate an immediate HVAC ventilation shutoff (flow to 0 cm/s) on detecting smoke or flame radiation, before discharging the extinguishing agent.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Localized nitrogen suppression (BASS)
investigador_responsable: Equipo BASS
material_combustible: PMMA spheres and plates
condiciones: Local N2 jet applied to a burning sample
descripcion_objetivo: A local nitrogen jet can strengthen the flame and keep it alive even after the main flow is turned off
consecuencia_hallazgo: Where to apply the suppressant is not obvious in microgravity; a misdirected jet entrains oxygen toward the flame
modificaciones_necesarias: Redesign extinguisher nozzles with total-flooding diffusers or enveloping mist instead of narrow inert-gas jets that induce O2 mixing.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Cool flames and spontaneous reignition (FLEX)
investigador_responsable: Equipo FLEX
material_combustible: Liquid hydrocarbon fuels
condiciones: After the visible hot flame goes out
descripcion_objetivo: After the visible flame goes out, a cool flame can keep burning and reignite spontaneously
consecuencia_hallazgo: Fire invisible to the naked eye; high risk of late reignition
modificaciones_necesarias: Add mid-wave IR cameras and CO/formaldehyde sensors to verify complete chemical (not just visual) extinction after a fire.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Smoke detection in microgravity (SAME, DAFT)
investigador_responsable: SAME and DAFT hardware
material_combustible: Space cabin materials
condiciones: No natural convection -> longer smoke residence time
descripcion_objetivo: Smoke particle size in microgravity is very different from that on Earth
consecuencia_hallazgo: Terrestrial detectors would look for the wrong signal
modificaciones_necesarias: Recalibrate optical scattering angles and detection algorithms for the large agglomerated particles typical of microgravity.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Ease of ignition in low gravity
investigador_responsable: NASA GRC Flammability Team
material_combustible: Cabin polymers and composites
condiciones: Low gravity / microgravity with external radiation
descripcion_objetivo: Materials ignite more easily in low gravity; the critical heat flux can be half
consecuencia_hallazgo: Higher ignition risk from electrical overloads or radiant sources
modificaciones_necesarias: Halve the maximum allowed temperature/heat flux on surfaces near cables and batteries; reinforce fast-acting circuit breakers.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Debunking 3 misconceptions about fire in space
investigador_responsable: Summary of the NASA safety chapter
material_combustible: Gases, liquids and solids in microgravity
condiciones: Quiescent microgravity and slow flow
descripcion_objetivo: It was believed that a steady fire cannot exist without convection, that it self-extinguishes without ventilation, and that terrestrial standards are conservative
consecuencia_hallazgo: All three assumptions proved false in real orbital tests
modificaciones_necesarias: Update all crew training manuals and aerospace engineering standards to remove the 3 false assumptions.

experimento_investigacion: Finding: Water-mist extinguishers on the ISS (Mist)
investigador_responsable: Equipo Mist / ISS Program
material_combustible: Class A/B/C cabin fires on the ISS
condiciones: Fine water-mist discharge in microgravity
descripcion_objetivo: Water-mist extinguishers were developed; the first two of nine reached the ISS in Dec. 2015
consecuencia_hallazgo: Definitive replacement of CO2 units in the US segment of the ISS
modificaciones_necesarias: Standardize water-mist extinguishers in orbital modules to avoid a lethal CO2 build-up after a discharge.

experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: MHD flow and nucleation in Zr64Ni36 (Cycles 9, 19, 22, 23, 26, 29)
categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker (WPI / UMass), D. M. Matson, K. F. Kelton
material_combustible: Molten metal alloy Zr64Ni36 (8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 7.271e5 S/m)
condiciones: Electromagnetic levitation in microgravity; T = 1040-1760 K; heater current 17.5-55.7 A; positioner 140.8-191.7 A; 458 CFD files + 2 telemetry CSVs in part-01
descripcion_objetivo: Characterize MHD flow velocity, Reynolds number and shear-strain rate during cooling to recalescence, to study cavitation/flow-induced dynamic nucleation
consecuencia_hallazgo: In Cycles 19, 22, 23 the flow is laminar (Re = 0.69-0.92, shear = 5.6-6.5 1/s); in Cycles 26 and 29, with the heater on, the flow is initially turbulent (Re > 600 above 1720 K and 1460 K) and crosses the laminar-turbulent transition; the cooling rate (0.02-1.33 °C/s) was an order of magnitude lower than in the SRD (10 °C/s)
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Switch from the laminar model to the RNG k-epsilon turbulent model above 1460 K (Cycle 29) and 1720 K (Cycle 26); 2) Recalculate the target shear-strain rate for the real slow cooling rates (0.02-1.33 °C/s) so that concentration profiles around subcritical nuclei do not interact; 3) Turn off the heater control voltage (0.000 V) during the free-cooling phase.
fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Reports_Updated ZrNi Report.pdf & 458 archivos Raw Data ZrNi

experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Flow characterization in Cu50Zr50 (Cycles 3, 4, 9, 10, 16, 18)
categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker (WPI / UMass)
material_combustible: Metallic-glass-forming alloy Cu50Zr50 (6.5 mm sphere, sigma = 7.05e5 S/m)
condiciones: T = 950-1455 K; heater 0.000 V (17.5 A); positioner 1.498-6.659 V (70.3-215.6 A); 256 CFD files in part-01
descripcion_objetivo: Correlate EML coil voltage with maximum velocity and shear rate near the liquidus temperature and recalescence (950-1075 K)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Fully laminar flow throughout cooling (Re = 0.007 to 1.44 << 600; shear-strain = 0.519 to 5.41 1/s), but the real cooling rate (0.31 to 2.01 K/s) was much slower than the 10 K/s specified in the SRD
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Review and recalculate the shear-strain-rate target specific to Cu50Zr50 at low cooling rates (0.31-2.01 K/s), considering its own chemical and thermodynamic driving forces; 2) Prefer the low positioner-voltage setup (1.498 V, Cycles 9-10) to minimize pole-equator asymmetry (2.7x vs 24x in Cycles 3-4).
fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Analyzed Data_Additiaonal CuZr Simulation Results.pdf & 256 archivos Raw Data Cu50Zr50

experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Quasicrystal nucleation in Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, 64, 65, 66)
categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker, K. F. Kelton (Washington U.)
material_combustible: Quasicrystal-forming alloy Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (6.0 mm sphere, liquidus 1093 K)
condiciones: Undercooling of ~150 K (recalescence at 980-1032 K); positioner 3.87-9.39 V; 12 FluentMagData zip files and 3 reports in part-01
descripcion_objetivo: Check whether the shear-strain rate meets the SRD requirement to avoid collisions between the diffusion fields of critical and subcritical nuclei
consecuencia_hallazgo: Laminar flow (Re = 0.30-1.33), but the shear-strain rate (3.10-9.45 1/s) exceeds the strict subcritical-cluster limit (0.05-0.5 1/s); also, Cycles 64-66 cooled 2.5-3x faster (-25.5 to -30.9 K/s) and the other 6 cycles much slower (-2.18 to -7.95 K/s) than the SRD's 10 K/s
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalculate the SRD shear-strain-rate targets separately for the fast-cooling (Cycles 64-66, ~28 K/s) and slow-cooling cycles (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, ~2-8 K/s); 2) Lower the positioner voltage in Cycles 65-66 (from 9.39 V to <= 3.87 V) to bring the shear rate down toward the diffusion-controlled regime (0.05-0.5 1/s).

experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Turbulence and viscosity in Sb-doped molten germanium (Ge Batch 2.1)
categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
investigador_responsable: G. P. Bracker, R. W. Hyers (for the SEMITHERM group / Samwer & Luo)
material_combustible: Antimony (Sb)-doped germanium (10^19 /cm3, 8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 1.52e6 S/m)
condiciones: T = 1158-1310 K; oscillating-drop method; 33 Raw Data Ge files and Final Ge Report.pdf in part-01
descripcion_objetivo: Explain the 1 to 2 orders-of-magnitude discrepancy between the viscosity measured in ISS-EML (0.0029 Pa·s), parabolic flights (0.0124-0.0136 Pa·s) and a rotating cup on Earth (4.55e-4 Pa·s)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Both the video of chaotic oxide rafts and the CFD model show the flow is highly turbulent throughout the cycle (Re = 69,400-72,700 at maximum T and Re = 6,450-6,600 just before recalescence), damping the oscillations and artificially inflating the apparent viscosity
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Modify the oscillating-drop damping equation to include turbulent eddy viscosity (from the RNG k-epsilon model) so turbulent damping is discounted; 2) Drastically reduce positioning and heating currents for highly conductive semiconductor samples (1.52e6 S/m).

experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Simulation stability and flow in Vit106 metallic glass (Cycles 1, 8, 60, 68)
categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
investigador_responsable: G. P. Bracker, R. W. Hyers
material_combustible: Bulk-metallic-glass-forming alloy Vit106 (sigma = 6.00e5 S/m)
condiciones: Recalescence at 850-875 K; high viscosity (8.37-15.1 Pa·s); cooling rates of 0.85 to 19.63 °C/s
descripcion_objetivo: Characterize extremely slow flow in a very viscous undercooled liquid down to recalescence
consecuencia_hallazgo: At low temperatures the VFT viscosity fit grows excessively and makes the CFD simulations numerically unstable; with the KKZNT fit the flow is stable and ultra-laminar (Re = 4.49e-5 to 7.23e-4; shear-strain = 0.031 to 0.274 1/s)
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace the VFT viscosity law with the KKZNT formulation using a Heaviside step function at low temperatures (T < T* = 1471.7 K) to ensure numerical stability in ANSYS Fluent; 2) Recalculate the shear-strain-rate target for each cycle's cooling rate (0.85 to 19.63 °C/s).

codigo_corto: PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-25: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II) in the ISS MSG
categoria: Sólidos / inflamabilidad y supresión en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-25)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / modified SPICE flow duct (7.6 x 7.6 cm section)
investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien (CWRU), C. Fernandez-Pello (UC Berkeley), I. S. Wichman (MSU), F. J. Miller (SDSU)
fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 38-40 (2014) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-25
material_combustible: Flat black and clear PMMA plates (1.2-6.35 mm), PMMA cylinders (6.35-12.7 mm), PMMA spheres (19 mm), SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), thin cotton, Nomex and Ultem film
condiciones: Opposed and concurrent forced flow from 0 to 53 cm/s (high sensitivity at 0.4-10 cm/s); N2 vitiation from 21.8% down to 13.5% O2 (MOC/LOI determination); cabin pressure ~100.5-101.5 kPa; radiometer, thermocouples and HD video
descripcion_objetivo: Determine flame spread rates (Vf), radiative extinction limits (low flow) and convective blowoff limits (high flow), and compare the limiting oxygen index (MOC) in 0 g with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
consecuencia_hallazgo: PMMA and SIBAL fabric samples sustain stable faint blue flames at ultra-low flows (0.5-2 cm/s) with O2 concentrations up to 2.5-3.5% below the 1 g terrestrial limit; stepping the fan down (step-down flow) reveals thermal hysteresis before radiative extinction
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Lower the MOC certification threshold for cabin polymers and textiles to <= 15.0% O2 for slow-ventilation regimes (0.5-8 cm/s); 2) Add two-branch extinction curves (radiative quenching < 1 cm/s and convective blowoff > 30 cm/s) to the Orion/Gateway fire code; 3) Require a waiting time after ventilation shutoff (> 60 s) because of the thermal inertia of thick solids (PMMA >= 3.2 mm).

experimento_investigacion: PSI-68: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
categoria: Combustión de gotas aisladas, mezclas bicomponente y llamas frías (Repositorio NASA PSI-68)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), F. L. Dryer (Princeton), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Dietrich & M. C. Hicks (NASA GRC), T. I. Farouk (USC)
fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 29-45 (2012-2015) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-68
material_combustible: Free or SiC-fiber-supported liquid droplets (D0 = 1.8 to 5.0 mm): n-heptane, n-decane, n-octane, n-dodecane, methanol, ethanol, PRF blends (n-heptane/iso-octane), jet-fuel surrogates (decane/propylbenzene) and binary droplet arrays
condiciones: Ambient pressure 0.5 to 3.0 atm (50.6 to 304.0 kPa); O2 concentration 12% to 40%; N2, CO2, He and Xe diluents; quiescent environment (0 cm/s) and slow convective flow by translation (0.5 to 22 cm/s); droplet spacing L/D0 = 2 to 12
descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the burning-rate constant K (d^2 law: D^2 = D0^2 - K*t), soot-shell formation, radiative extinction of the hot flame, transition to two-stage combustion (cool flames at 550-750 K) and droplet-droplet interaction
consecuencia_hallazgo: Large linear alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) undergo radiative extinction of the visible hot flame but keep vaporizing through invisible cool flames governed by NTC (negative temperature coefficient) chemistry, which can produce an explosive vapour-cloud reignition; in alcohols (methanol/ethanol), absorption of the water produced in the flame causes abrupt extinction
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K); 2) Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats; 3) Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons.

experimento_investigacion: PSI-26: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) in the ISS MSG
categoria: Sólidos / inflamabilidad, propagación upwind y supresión con N2 (Repositorio NASA PSI-26)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / SPICE duct with N2 suppressant nozzle
investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien (CWRU), C. Fernandez-Pello, I. S. Wichman, F. J. Miller
fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 30-31 (2012) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-26
material_combustible: PMMA spheres (20 mm), flat PMMA plates (1.5 mm), paraffin and porous wax candles, SIBAL fabric (cotton/fiberglass)
condiciones: Cabin air (21% O2 down to 15.8% O2), 1 atm (100.4-101.3 kPa), forced flow from 0 to 35 cm/s and application of a localized N2 jet
descripcion_objetivo: Investigate burning and extinction of solid fuels in microgravity, upwind spread geometry and the effectiveness of nitrogen jets
consecuencia_hallazgo: Showed for the first time on the ISS that spread at low flows (<10 cm/s) happens only against the wind (upwind), that materials burn at lower O2 than in NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, and that a slow local N2 jet intensifies the flame by entraining surrounding O2
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Prohibit narrow N2-jet extinguisher nozzles without first cutting ventilation; 2) Reorient thermal sensors upstream of electronic components; 3) Replace the one-dimensional criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.

codigo_corto: PSI-62: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM & Two-Color Tomography)

instalacion_hardware: High-fidelity CFD simulation (UFGM / OpenFOAM / ANSYS) validated against ISS MSG video (BASS PSI-26 & BASS-II PSI-25)

codigo_corto: PSI-98: SAFFIRE-I (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-98: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I (SAFFIRE-I) on the Cygnus OA-6 vehicle
categoria: Incendio a gran escala en nave espacial real (Repositorio NASA PSI-98)
instalacion_hardware: Autonomous SAFFIRE module on the Northrop Grumman Cygnus OA-6 cargo vehicle (after undocking from the ISS)
investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), C. Fernandez-Pello, J. S. T'ien, S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul
fecha_periodo: June 2016 (Cygnus OA-6 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-98
material_combustible: Large continuous panel of SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 0.40 m wide x 0.94 m long
condiciones: Concurrent forced flow of 20 cm/s in a large-section flow tunnel; nominal air ~21% O2 and 101.3 kPa (1 atm); hot-wire ignition at the upstream and downstream edges
descripcion_objetivo: Characterize for the first time the growth of a large (~1 m) fire in real microgravity, checking whether the flame grows indefinitely or reaches a steady limiting size
consecuencia_hallazgo: Unlike terrestrial fires, which accelerate exponentially, in microgravity at 20 cm/s the flame quickly reached a steady limiting length (~20-25 cm) and a constant spread rate (~1.6 mm/s), owing to the radiative balance and O2 consumption in the boundary layer
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update cabin emergency-response models with the large-scale steady spread rate and the fast pressure/temperature rise in a closed volume; 2) Validate that cutting ventilation immediately stops a 0.4 m-wide flame front.

codigo_corto: PSI-99: SAFFIRE-II (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-99: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II (SAFFIRE-II, 9 samples) on the Cygnus OA-5 vehicle
categoria: Límites MOC de materiales estructurales y textiles a escala real (Repositorio NASA PSI-99)
instalacion_hardware: Autonomous SAFFIRE module on the Cygnus OA-5 cargo vehicle (sample holder with 9 panels of 5 cm x 29 cm)
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), Equipo Internacional SAFFIRE
fecha_periodo: November 2016 (Cygnus OA-5 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-99
material_combustible: 9 samples (5 x 29 cm): SIBAL fabric, Nomex HT90-40, silicone sheets of 3 thicknesses (0.25, 0.60 and 1.57 mm), 10 mm PMMA plates, flat and with longitudinal grooved ribs, and cotton fabric
condiciones: Forced flows of 20 cm/s and 30 cm/s; cabin atmosphere (~20.8-21.0% O2 initially, falling progressively to ~17.2% O2 through consumption in the Cygnus module); ~101.0 kPa
descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate the effect of material thickness, surface geometry (grooves/edges) and O2 decline on flammability in microgravity versus NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
consecuencia_hallazgo: The thin silicone sheets (0.25 and 0.60 mm) burned vigorously while the thick one (1.57 mm) went out; the machined grooves in the thick PMMA (10 mm) acted as thermal fins that sustained spread where an identical flat plate self-extinguished
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Penalize in certification protocols geometries with exposed edges, grooves or ribs in thick polymers (PMMA/polycarbonate), since they sustain the flame when the flat surface does not burn; 2) Restrict silicone membranes thinner than 1.5 mm in ducts with flow >= 20 cm/s.

codigo_corto: PSI-100: SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-100: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III (SAFFIRE-III) on the Cygnus OA-7 vehicle
categoria: Efecto de alta velocidad de ventilación en incendio a gran escala (Repositorio NASA PSI-100)

investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), C. Fernandez-Pello, J. S. T'ien
fecha_periodo: June 2017 (Cygnus OA-7 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-100
material_combustible: Large continuous panel of SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass, 0.40 m x 0.94 m)
condiciones: Concurrent forced flow raised to 30 cm/s (50% higher than in SAFFIRE-I); ~20.9% O2, 101.3 kPa; CO2, O2, pressure and radiometry measurements

codigo_corto: PSI-101: SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-101: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight (SAME-R) in the ISS MSG
categoria: Distribución de tamaño y envejecimiento de aerosoles de humo espacial (Repositorio NASA PSI-101)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with PAMS (particle counter), aerosol moment meter, ionization (ISS smoke detector) and laser scattering (Orion smoke detector)
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), G. W. Mulholland (NIST / U. Maryland), T. Cleary (NIST)
fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 23-24 (2010) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-101
material_combustible: Samples pyrolyzed by thermal overload: Kapton and Teflon (PTFE) wire insulation, silicone rubber, cellulose paper, PMMA and lamp-oil wick
condiciones: Duct flow velocities of 1.5 to 6.0 cm/s; controlled aerosol aging (aging chamber, 0 to 600 s); ~20.9% O2, 101.3 kPa
descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the count median diameter (CMD), Sauter mean diameter (SMD) and aging coagulation of smoke from spacecraft materials to calibrate the ISS and Orion smoke detectors
consecuencia_hallazgo: In microgravity the lack of a buoyant plume keeps pyrolyzed vapour near the hot source longer, producing primary particles and agglomerates significantly larger (CMD 0.3 to 1.2 microns) than in 1 g, which lowers the sensitivity of conventional ionization detectors and favours laser-scattering optical ones
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace ionization smoke detectors (designed for ultrafine particles < 0.1 microns in 1 g) with laser-scattering photoelectric detectors calibrated for the 0.3-1.5 micron range measured in SAME-R; 2) Include coagulation-compensation algorithms for slow transport through the cabin.

categoria: Generación y detección temprana de humo por pirólisis en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-102)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / ISS smoke detector (ionization) and Space Shuttle detector (photoelectric) + TEM thermal precipitator
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), G. W. Mulholland, Z. G. Yuan, T. Cleary
fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 15 (July 2007) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-102
material_combustible: Teflon (PTFE), Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose (paper) and lamp oil (lamp oil wick)
condiciones: Flameless pyrolysis (non-flaming overheat) at different heating powers and ventilation flows of 1.0 to 7.0 cm/s; direct sampling onto transmission electron microscopy (TEM) grids
descripcion_objetivo: Establish the baseline fractal morphology and size-distribution moments of smoke from aerospace materials to compare the response of the Shuttle and ISS detectors
consecuencia_hallazgo: Overheated Teflon produces ultrafine particles (~0.06-0.12 microns) invisible to the standard optical detector without coagulation, while silicone and cellulose produce large fractal chains (>0.5 microns) that saturate the photoelectric sensor before the ionization one
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Deploy dual-wavelength (blue + near-infrared) smoke sensors that measure the size-moment ratio (mean diameter) at the same time, to tell Teflon/wire pyrolysis (small particles) from silicone/cellulose smoke or ambient dust.

experimento_investigacion: PSI-10: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Flame Design (ACME) in the ISS CIR
categoria: Llamas de difusión esféricas normales e inversas y control estequiométrico de hollín (Repositorio NASA PSI-10)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME insert with a porous spherical burner
investigador_responsable: R. L. Axelbaum (Washington U. in St. Louis), P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2019-2020 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-10
material_combustible: Ethylene (C2H4) and methane (CH4) with N2 dilution in normal (fuel inside) and inverse (oxidizer inside) diffusion-flame configurations
condiciones: Stoichiometric mixture fraction Z_st varied between 0.06 and 0.65 (O2 from 15.6% to 40%); pressure 1 atm (101.3 kPa); quiescent 6.4 mm porous spherical burner

modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Reconfigure space burners and incinerators by moving the diluent (N2/CO2) into the fuel stream to raise Z_st > 0.35, eliminating soot and excess thermal radiation even in O2-enriched exploration atmospheres.

experimento_investigacion: PSI-21: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME CLD) in the ISS CIR

material_combustible: Methane and ethylene highly diluted with N2 in air coflow in the CIR
condiciones: Coflow velocity 2 to 30 cm/s; N2 dilution of the fuel up to the liftoff and blowoff limits; pressure 101.3 kPa
descripcion_objetivo: Study the coupled chemical-fluid structure of lifted and sooting flames in microgravity to validate C1-C2 hydrocarbon kinetic mechanisms at dilution extremes
consecuencia_hallazgo: Without buoyant acceleration, the base of the lifted flame (triple flame) stabilizes at much lower velocities and depends purely on the stoichiometric laminar flame speed and radiative losses
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalibrate the edge/triple-flame stabilization and soot-radiation sub-models in CFD codes for low-emission combustors and space burners.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-21

codigo_corto: PSI-22: ACME / E-FIELD Flames (Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-22: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME E-FIELD) in the ISS CIR
categoria: Control electrohidrodinámico (EHD) de llamas y viento iónico en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-22)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / coaxial burner with a high-voltage electrode mesh (up to +/- 10 kV) and an ion-current ammeter
investigador_responsable: D. Dunn-Rankin (UC Irvine), F. J. Weinberg (Imperial College), Z. G. Yuan (NASA GRC)
fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2018-2019 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-22
material_combustible: Methane and ethylene (pure and N2-diluted) in a free jet or laminar coflow
condiciones: Applied voltage 0 to +/- 10 kV between burner and collector mesh; measurement of chemi-ionization saturation current (H3O+, CHO+, charged soot particles); 1 atm
descripcion_objetivo: Understand the relationship between electric-field voltage, chemical ion current and the induced ionic wind to control flame stability, length and soot emission in microgravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Without terrestrial buoyancy interfering, the electric field accelerates the ions formed in the reaction zone, dragging neutral molecules (ionic wind); this shortens the flame, suppresses soot completely and allows variable artificial gravity to be emulated
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add high-voltage electrode rings/meshes (6-9 kV, < 1 W) to orbital burners and incinerators to replace mechanical fans with ionic-wind convection and eliminate soot emission.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-22

codigo_corto: PSI-23: ACME / s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-23: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME s-Flame) in the ISS CIR
categoria: Dinámica unidimensional, inestabilidad pulsante y extinción radiativa en llamas esféricas (Repositorio NASA PSI-23)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / 6.4 mm porous spherical burner fed with H2, CH4 and C2H4
investigador_responsable: C. K. Law (Princeton University), S. H. Tse (Rutgers), R. L. Axelbaum (WUSTL)
fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2017-2018 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-23
material_combustible: Soot-free (hydrogen H2 and methane CH4) and sooting (ethylene C2H4) mixtures diluted with He, N2, Ar or CO2
condiciones: Pure 1D spherical geometry in microgravity; effective Lewis number (Le) varied with helium/argon/CO2; mass flows of 0.3 to 5.0 mg/s
descripcion_objetivo: Isolate the coupling between preferential diffusion (Lewis number), gas/soot radiative losses and pulsating instabilities before radiative or diffusive extinction
consecuencia_hallazgo: Large-amplitude pulsating oscillations were observed near the radiative extinction limit when the Lewis number exceeds the critical threshold (Le > 1), confirming theoretical predictions impossible to observe in 1 g
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include pulsating diffusive-thermal instability criteria (Le > 1) and CO2/H2O radiative reabsorption in spherical fire spread and extinction models for space cabins.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-23

experimento_investigacion: PSI-39: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
categoria: Química de baja temperatura y combustión en dos etapas de hidrocarburos pesados y ésteres (Repositorio NASA PSI-39)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Dietrich & M. C. Hicks (NASA GRC), F. L. Dryer (Princeton)
fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2013-2017 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-39
material_combustible: Droplets of n-decane, n-dodecane, heptane/iso-octane blends and methyl butanoate (biodiesel surrogate)
condiciones: Droplets of 0.8 to 4.5 mm; pressures of 1.0 to 3.0 atm (101.3 to 304.0 kPa); O2 from 14% to 30% in N2/CO2; intensified UV (OH*) and visible/blue (HCHO*) cameras
descripcion_objetivo: Systematically investigate the hot-to-cool flame transition regime (NTC, 550-800 K), second-stage induction times and diffusive extinction of cool flames
consecuencia_hallazgo: Showed that while C7-C12 linear alkanes sustain long cool flames after radiative extinction of the hot flame, submillimetre oxygenated esters such as methyl butanoate show suppression of the NTC branch
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Differentiate in-orbit safety and suppression protocols by the liquid's molecular structure (linear alkanes with a high risk of invisible cool flames vs esters/alcohols without an NTC branch).
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-39

codigo_corto: PSI-47: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-47: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test 1 & 2 (DAFT / DAFT-2) in the ISS cabin
categoria: Conteo de partículas ultrafinas en cabina y viabilidad de fluidos capilares para P-Trak (Repositorio NASA PSI-47)
instalacion_hardware: ISS cabin (USOS and Russian segments) / commercial TSI P-Trak condensation particle counter (CPC) modified for microgravity
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), Risk Mitigation Team for SAME (PSI-102)
fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 12-16 (2006-2007) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-47
material_combustible: ISS cabin background aerosol and ultrafine particles (< 0.1 microns) from crew activities and incipient combustion; isopropyl alcohol working fluid in a capillary wick
condiciones: Ambient sampling in several ISS modules; cabin airflow 5 to 12 cm/s; capillary saturation test of the P-Trak wick in 0 g
descripcion_objetivo: Verify that the TSI P-Trak condensation particle counter works correctly with capillary transport in microgravity (mitigating the risk for SAME PSI-102) and measure the background ultrafine-particle level on the ISS
consecuencia_hallazgo: Capillary alcohol transport worked in 0 g; it was also found that the background ultrafine-particle concentration on the ISS is extremely low (< 100-500 particles/cm3 thanks to HEPA filters) except for sharp peaks during food cooking/heating, which gives an excellent signal-to-noise ratio for detecting early fires
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Exploit the low cabin background of ultrafine particles (thanks to HEPA filtering) by setting early pre-alarm thresholds on condensation-nucleus counts (CPC) for incipient electrical overloads; 2) Temporarily mask the pre-alarm in the food-warmer (galley) area.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-47

codigo_corto: PSI-60: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data
experimento_investigacion: PSI-60: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Datasets (derived from PSI-107)
categoria: Modelado CFD de punto de humo, oxidación de hollín y apertura de punta radiativa (Repositorio NASA PSI-60)
instalacion_hardware: 2D/axisymmetric CFD simulation + SPICE experimental database from the ISS MSG (PSI-107)
investigador_responsable: P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), NASA PSI-60 grant investigators
material_combustible: Ethylene, propylene, propane and n-butane in laminar air coflow
condiciones: Nozzles of 1.1 to 4.1 mm; coflow velocities of 1 to 32 cm/s; transition from a closed soot-free flame to an open flame releasing soot at the tip (tip opening)
descripcion_objetivo: Numerically model soot nucleation, surface growth and O2/OH oxidation in microgravity coflow flames to explain why the smoke point in 0 g is much lower than in 1 g
consecuencia_hallazgo: In microgravity the residence time in the high-temperature annular region is much longer, and radiative cooling of the tip quenches the soot oxidation zone (radiative tip quenching), releasing wings of unburned soot
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Couple optically thin/thick radiation models with OH- and O2-radical soot oxidation kinetics to predict sudden soot release (wing/tip opening) in space fires.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-60

codigo_corto: PSI-106: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-106: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE) in the ISS MSG
categoria: Estabilización, estructura de borde y desprendimiento (liftoff) de llamas en coflujo (Repositorio NASA PSI-106)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / reconfigured SPICE hardware with color digital cameras and CH*/OH*/C2* filters
investigador_responsable: M. B. Long, M. D. Smooke (Yale University), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 30-31 (2012) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-106

condiciones: Attached and lifted flames at coflow velocities of 1.5 to 30 cm/s; acoustic/pulsed disturbances
descripcion_objetivo: Investigate the structure of partially premixed flames at the liftoff base (liftoff height) and the blowout limit without buoyancy
consecuencia_hallazgo: Provided the first quantitative maps of CH* and C2* radical luminescence together with soot pyrometry in lifted flames on the ISS, a direct bridge to the design of ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21)
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Design flame holders in space combustion systems taking into account that liftoff height in 0 g is more sensitive to the coflow momentum deficit.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-106

codigo_corto: PSI-107: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-107: Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment (SPICE) in the ISS MSG
categoria: Determinación experimental del punto de humeo (smoke point) en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-107)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / miniature wind tunnel with hot-wire anemometry and a retractable igniter
investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), G. M. Faeth (U. Michigan), Z. G. Yuan
fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 18-19 (2009) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-107
material_combustible: Six gaseous hydrocarbons: methane, propane, n-butane, ethylene, propylene and blends in air coflow
condiciones: Nozzle diameters of 1.1, 2.0 and 4.1 mm; air coflow velocity 0.8 to 35 cm/s; cabin pressure 101.3 kPa, ~21% O2
descripcion_objetivo: Determine the luminous flame length and the critical fuel flow at the transition from a soot-free to a soot-emitting flame (smoke point) in microgravity
consecuencia_hallazgo: Smoke points in microgravity are 2 to 5 times lower than in terrestrial gravity, owing to the lack of buoyant acceleration and radiative quenching of the flame tip; raising the coflow velocity restores tip oxidation and raises the smoke-point threshold
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Apply a 3x safety reduction factor to terrestrial smoke-point tables (ASTM D1322) when assessing soot propensity and HEPA filter loading in space fires.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-107

codigo_corto: PSI-108: STDCE-1 (Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-108: Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1 (STDCE-1) on USML-1 STS-50
categoria: Convección termocapilar de Marangoni e hidrodinámica de superficies libres calientes (Repositorio NASA PSI-108)
instalacion_hardware: Spacelab USML-1 (Space Shuttle Columbia STS-50) / 10 cm cylindrical chamber with CO2 laser heating (CT) and an immersed heater (CF) + IR thermography and PIV
investigador_responsable: S. Ostrach, Y. Kamotani (Case Western Reserve University), A. Pline (NASA GRC)
fecha_periodo: June-July 1992 (STS-50) and PIV reanalysis in NASA PSI-108
material_combustible: 10 cSt silicone fluid with 50-micron alumina tracers on flat and curved free surfaces
condiciones: Surface thermal gradients of 5 to 60 °C; heating powers of 0.5 to 30 W; Marangoni number (Ma) up to 10^5 and high thermocapillary Reynolds number
descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the velocity and structure of thermocapillary convection vortices (Marangoni effect) driven by surface-tension gradients without buoyant natural convection
consecuencia_hallazgo: Thermocapillary flow fully dominates heat and mass transport in free-surface liquids in microgravity, controlling the preheating rate in liquid fuel pools, burning droplets and solder/melt pools
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include Marangoni thermocapillary shear-stress boundary conditions (d_sigma/dT) in flame-spread models over liquids and molten polymer pools in microgravity.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-108

codigo_corto: PSI-115: Advanced modelling of smoke generation (SAME data)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-115: Utilization of SAME Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Microgravity
categoria: Simulación numérica de balance poblacional y coagulación de aerosoles de humo en 0-g (Repositorio NASA PSI-115)
instalacion_hardware: CFD-PBM (population balance modelling) coupled with experimental data from SAME (PSI-102) and SAME-R (PSI-101)
investigador_responsable: NASA PSI-115 grant investigators / collaboration with the NASA GRC Smoke Detection Team
material_combustible: Pyrolysis aerosols from Kapton, Teflon (PTFE), silicone rubber, cellulose and PMMA
condiciones: General dynamic equation for aerosols (GDE) with homogeneous nucleation, condensation, fractal Brownian coagulation and thermophoretic deposition in a 1 to 7 cm/s duct
descripcion_objetivo: Develop predictive tools for the generation and size evolution of smoke particles in microgravity using the SAME empirical database (PSI-102)
consecuencia_hallazgo: The model shows that the fractal dimension (Df ~ 1.7-1.9) and the lack of buoyant dilution at the source speed up the quadratic coagulation rate by 4x to 8x relative to 1 g, shifting the log-normal distribution toward larger diameters
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Integrate the aerosol population-balance module (PBM with fractal dimension 1.8) into habitat ventilation simulation software (Orion/Gateway) to optimize the placement of photoelectric detectors.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-115

codigo_corto: PSI-117: Multiphysics CFD dynamics of cool flames under thermoconvective perturbation
experimento_investigacion: PSI-117: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multiphysics Multidimensional CFD Analysis
categoria: Análisis CFD 2D/3D de llamas frías en gotas y sprays bajo perturbaciones convectivas (Repositorio NASA PSI-117)
instalacion_hardware: Multidimensional multiphysics CFD simulation validated with orbital data from FLEX (PSI-69) and counterflow (PSI-142)
investigador_responsable: T. I. Farouk (U. South Carolina), F. L. Dryer, NASA PSI-117 grant investigators
material_combustible: n-heptane, n-decane and dodecane droplets and aerosols under spray-relevant conditions
condiciones: External convective velocity perturbations (0.5 to 25 cm/s) and thermal pulses; pressures of 1.0 to 3.0 atm; reduced skeletal kinetics with low-temperature chemistry (RO2 / QOOH)
descripcion_objetivo: Determine how multidimensional asymmetries induced by external convective flows or droplet interaction change cool-flame stability and trigger hot reignition
consecuencia_hallazgo: A moderate convective perturbation accumulates intermediate species (peroxides and hydroperoxides) in the wake downstream of the droplet, which can cause an explosive secondary reignition to a hot flame, while an intense vortex breaks the NTC envelope and extinguishes the cool flame
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Avoid sudden ventilation pulses over post-extinction hydrocarbon vapour clouds, since the convective wake concentrates RO2/H2O2 radicals and triggers secondary hot reignition.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-117

codigo_corto: PSI-142: Cool-flame transitions in radiative and strain extinction
experimento_investigacion: PSI-142: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions in Radiative/Stretch Extinction using Counterflow Flames
categoria: Cinética cuantitativa de transición llama caliente/fría en contracorriente y fluidos reactivos (Repositorio NASA PSI-142)
investigador_responsable: Y. Ju (Princeton University), F. L. Dryer, NASA PSI-142 team
material_combustible: Heavy alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) and esters in counterflow diffusion and premixed configurations
condiciones: Aerodynamic strain rates of 5 to 300 1/s; controlled radiative losses; pressures of 1 to 3 atm
descripcion_objetivo: Map the extended two-branch S-curve (hot flame and cool flame) to quantify the exact transition limits by radiation (low strain) and by aerodynamic strain (high strain)
consecuencia_hallazgo: Established the unified four-branch S-curve flammability regimes, showing that the cool-flame branch survives strain rates and radiative losses at which the hot flame collapses
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update strain-extinction criteria (critical Damköhler number) in space engines and suppression systems using the 4-branch S-curve that includes the cool-flame regime.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-142

codigo_corto: PSI-159: ACME / CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-159: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G) in the ISS CIR
categoria: Llamas frías de difusión puramente gaseosas en quemador esférico poroso (Repositorio NASA PSI-159)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME porous spherical burner with intensified UV/visible cameras
investigador_responsable: P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), R. L. Axelbaum (WUSTL), C. K. Law (Princeton), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Urban
fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2021 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-159
material_combustible: Gaseous fuels: n-butane, propane and vaporized n-pentane diluted with N2 in an enriched atmosphere or air
condiciones: Spherical burner with no liquid phase or free edge; pressures of 1.0 to 2.5 atm (101.3 to 253 kPa); O2 from 15% to 30%; long observation times (minutes)
descripcion_objetivo: Achieve for the first time steady diffusion cool flames with purely gaseous fuels (no liquid droplets) in microgravity, to isolate gas-phase NTC chemistry from the liquid-vapour phase change
consecuencia_hallazgo: Confirmed experimentally in the CIR that stable spherical cool flames of gaseous n-butane and n-pentane exist for several minutes, supporting the design of cleaner, more efficient HCCI/RCCI internal-combustion engines
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Extend cool-flame detection protocols (HCHO* and CO sensors) to leaks of light gaseous hydrocarbons (propane, butane, pentane) in space thermal and propulsion systems.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-159

codigo_corto: PSI-181: Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solders in microgravity and extreme temperatures (ISSI)
experimento_investigacion: PSI-181: Structure and Properties of Pb-Sn and Lead-Free Sn-Ag-Cu Solders in Terrestrial vs. Microgravity under Extreme Temperatures
categoria: Confiabilidad termo-eléctrica de soldaduras espaciales, atrapamiento de poros y prevención de sobrecalentamiento/arcos (Repositorio NASA PSI-181)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG - In-Space Soldering Investigation ISSI PSI-77) + cryogenic/elevated thermal cycling on Earth
investigador_responsable: R. N. Grugel (NASA MSFC), NASA PSI-181 grant investigators
fecha_periodo: ISSI on the ISS (2004-2005) / PSI-181 microstructural and thermal study (2020-2023)
material_combustible: Electronic solder alloys: eutectic Pb-Sn and lead-free Sn-Ag-Cu (SAC305) with organic Rosin flux
condiciones: Manual soldering and reflow in microgravity; thermal cycling from cryogenic (-196 °C) to elevated (+150 °C) temperatures; analysis of porosity and Cu6Sn5 / Ag3Sn intermetallic phases
descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate how the lack of buoyancy in microgravity traps flux vapour bubbles inside Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solder joints, affecting electrical resistance, heat transfer and failure at extreme temperatures
consecuencia_hallazgo: Joints soldered in microgravity retain large gas voids (porosity up to 5-10x higher than in 1 g), which reduces the effective electrical/thermal conduction section, creates Joule hot spots (risk of wire pyrolysis/ignition) and accelerates thermomechanical fracture under cryogenic cycling
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Use solder wire without a volatile flux core, or apply vacuum/ultrasonic degassing during in-orbit electronic repairs (in-space manufacturing/repair), to avoid trapped pores that create hot spots and electrical ignition; 2) Prefer doped SAC formulations with intermetallic control for lunar missions with cryogenic cycling.
fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-181 (derived from PSI-77)

codigo_corto: SAFFIRE IV-VI & SoFIE SEA: Lunar/Martian atmospheres (8.2 psia / 34% O2)
experimento_investigacion: SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI & SoFIE (GEL/MIST/SMuRF) in space exploration atmospheres (8.2 psia / 56.5 kPa and 34% O2)
categoria: Incendios a gran escala y propagación en atmósferas de exploración Lunar Gateway / HLS / Marte (8.2 psia, 34% O2)
instalacion_hardware: Northrop Grumman Cygnus vehicles (SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI with Far-Field Diagnostics FFD) and ISS MSG (SoFIE)
investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban, P. V. Ferkul, S. L. Olson (NASA GRC) / Exploration Atmospheres Working Group (EAWG)
fecha_periodo: 2020-2024 (SAFFIRE IV-VI and SoFIE on the ISS) / NASA PSI & NTRS archive
material_combustible: Flat and grooved PMMA panels, SIBAL fabric, silicone membranes, Nomex, Ultem and Delrin
condiciones: Exploration atmosphere recommended by the NASA EAWG: reduced pressure of 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) and 34% O2 (or 10.2 psia / 70.3 kPa and 26.5-32% O2) to eliminate pre-breathing before lunar/Martian EVAs
descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate how the combination of high oxygen concentration (34% O2), low pressure (56.5 kPa) and partial gravity (0.16 g Moon / 0.38 g Mars) changes ignition, de Ris spread rate and the release of acid gases (CO, HCl, HF)
consecuencia_hallazgo: At 34% O2 and 56.5 kPa, fire-retardant materials that pass in standard air at 101.3 kPa (21% O2) sustain vigorous spread; the lower gas density reduces convective inertia, but the high O2 mole fraction raises the adiabatic flame temperature and speeds up de Ris heat transfer by a factor of 2.2x to 3.1x
modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Prohibit materials certified only at 21% O2 inside modules pressurized to 8.2 psia / 34% O2 (HLS, Gateway, lunar/Martian rovers); 2) Install far-field catalytic scrubbers (Far-Field Scrubbers for CO, CO2, HCl and HF tested in SAFFIRE IV-VI) and a rapid post-fire depressurization/repressurization protocol.
fuente: NASA PSI & NTRS - SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI & SoFIE Exploration Atmosphere Studies
referencia: https://psi.nasa.gov / NASA EAWG 8.2 psia 34% O2 Technical Reports

codigo_corto: SoFIE (ISS CIR - GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS, NCA)
experimento_investigacion: SoFIE — 5 official sub-projects in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) up to 37% O2 (8.2 psia SEA)
categoria: Inflamabilidad de combustibles sólidos en microgravedad y atmósferas de exploración Artemis SEA (34-37% O2)
instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) — GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS and NCA modules
investigador_responsable: J.S. T'ien (GEL), C. Fernandez-Pello (MIST), S. Olson (SMuRF), S. Bhattacharjee (RTDFS), F. Miller (NCA) — NASA GRC
material_combustible: PMMA spheres and cylinders, thin sheets, a thick plate in a narrow channel and real spacecraft materials
condiciones: 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) with a control band up to 37% O2 (and CIR mixtures up to 85% O2 / 15% N2) + external radiant heater (MIST)
descripcion_objetivo: Close the gap between 1 g ground tests (NASA-STD-6001B Test 1) and the real behaviour of spacecraft materials in microgravity and lunar/Martian atmospheres
consecuencia_hallazgo: External radiant flux (MIST) and narrow-channel confinement (NCA) sustain a flame even near the extinction limit, while SMuRF confirms that the terrestrial 15.2 cm criterion underestimates the risk at 37% O2
modificaciones_necesarias: Make the 5 SoFIE sub-projects a mandatory calibration reference for SEA atmospheres (34-37% O2) and radiative safety factors.
fuente: NASA Glenn Research Center - SoFIE (Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction)

experimento_investigacion: Standards: NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 (15.2 cm), JSC 20584 SMACs and NASA-STD-3001 dust/perchlorates
categoria: Certificación de materiales, toxicología post-incendio (HCl, HF, CO) y control de polvo lunar/marciano
instalacion_hardware: SAFFIRE IV-VI Far-Field Diagnostics (FFD), Smoke Eater, CO2/acid scrubber and HEPA filtration for Artemis/Mars
investigador_responsable: NASA Technical Standards & JSC Toxicology and Environmental Chemistry Lab
material_combustible: Non-metallic cabin materials + post-fire acid gases (HCl, HF, CO, HCN) + lunar dust (~0.1 mg/m3) and Martian perchlorates
condiciones: Vertical Test 1 (self-extinguishes < 15.2 cm / 6 in with no burning drips), 1 h/24 h/long-term SMACs (HF = 0.3 ppm) and additive index T_grp = sum(Ci/SMACi) < 1
descripcion_objetivo: Ensure material certification and post-fire toxicological survival of the crew in closed lunar and Martian habitats
consecuencia_hallazgo: Even when a fire goes out (as in SAFFIRE IV-VI), adsorption on aluminium walls and the additive toxicity of HF, HCl, CO and respirable regolith/perchlorate dust require active scrubbing ('Smoke Eater' + CO2/acid scrubber)
modificaciones_necesarias: Require T_grp < 1 verification after suppression, HEPA filtration <= 0.1 mg/m3 and HF/HCl acid-gas monitoring in Artemis and Mars habitats.
fuente: NASA Technical Standards (NASA-STD-6001B, NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2, JSC 20584)
